name: Business Weight Routing & Budget Integration
description: Use business weight for two purposes: (1) Token budget allocation — higher-weight contexts get proportionally larger share of the token budget. (2) Routing priority — in the BFS routing queue, order contexts by business weight so higher-weight contexts are evaluated first. Business weight affects evaluation ORDER only, never acceptance criteria, preserving stop-on-first-accept semantics. All functions are pure, fully type-annotated, and independently testable with no external service dependencies.

functions.name: validate_business_weight
functions.description: Validates and normalizes a raw business weight value. Values outside [0.0, 1.0] are rejected. Values in [0.0, 0.1) are clamped up to the operational floor of 0.1 (with a debug-level log). This is a pure function (the debug log is a trace-level side effect only).

inputs.name: raw_weight
inputs.description: The raw business weight value to validate and normalize.

error_data.message: business_weight must be a finite number, got {raw_weight}

postconditions: result >= 0.1 and result <= 1.0
if raw_weight >= 0.1 and raw_weight <= 1.0 then result == raw_weight
if raw_weight >= 0.0 and raw_weight < 0.1 then result == 0.1

functions.name: weighted_routing_order
functions.description: Returns contexts sorted by descending business_weight with stable tiebreaking (preserves original insertion order for equal weights). This is a pure function. It snapshots the weights from the input and produces an immutable ordering. business_weight is used ONLY for ordering — it MUST NOT influence familiarity scores, resonance checks, or acceptance thresholds.

inputs.name: contexts
inputs.description: The sequence of contexts to sort by business weight. May be empty.

error_data.note: Returns empty list — not an error.

error_cases.name: invalid_weight_in_context
error_cases.condition: Any context has a business_weight outside [0.0, 1.0]

preconditions: All contexts have valid business_weight values (in [0.1, 1.0] after validation).
postconditions: len(result) == len(contexts)
set of context_ids in result == set of context_ids in contexts
for all i < j: result[i].business_weight >= result[j].business_weight
for all i < j where result[i].business_weight == result[j].business_weight: original index of result[i] < original index of result[j] (stable sort)
No context is added, removed, or mutated — only order changes.

functions.name: create_routing_snapshot
functions.description: Creates an immutable routing snapshot by sorting the given contexts by descending business_weight with stable tiebreaking and freezing the ordering. Once created, the snapshot's ordered_contexts MUST NOT be re-sorted mid-round. This ensures deterministic evaluation order within a single routing round.

inputs.name: round_id
inputs.description: Unique identifier for the routing round.

inputs.name: contexts
inputs.description: The contexts to include in the snapshot.

inputs.name: snapshot_timestamp_ms
inputs.description: Millisecond-precision Unix timestamp at snapshot creation.

validators.error_message: snapshot_timestamp_ms must be a positive Unix timestamp.

error_data.message: round_id must be a non-empty string.
snapshot_timestamp_ms must be a positive integer.

error_cases.name: invalid_weight_in_context
error_cases.condition: Any context has a business_weight outside [0.0, 1.0]

preconditions: All contexts have valid business_weight values.
postconditions: result.round_id == round_id
result.snapshot_timestamp_ms == snapshot_timestamp_ms
result.ordered_contexts == weighted_routing_order(contexts)
result is immutable — ordered_contexts cannot be modified after creation.

functions.name: build_priority_queue
functions.description: Builds a heapq-compatible priority queue from a list of contexts. Each context is assigned a PriorityKey of (-business_weight, insertion_counter) where insertion_counter is the context's index in the input list. The result is a list of PriorityQueueEntry objects in heap order. This is an internal utility for the mesh routing layer.

inputs.name: contexts
inputs.description: Contexts to enqueue, in their original insertion order.

error_cases.name: invalid_weight_in_context
error_cases.condition: Any context has a business_weight outside [0.0, 1.0]

preconditions: All contexts have valid business_weight values (in [0.1, 1.0] after validation).
postconditions: len(result) == len(contexts)
result satisfies the min-heap invariant on (neg_weight, insertion_counter)
Popping from the heap yields contexts in descending business_weight order with stable tiebreaking.
Each entry's insertion_counter equals its original index in the input list.

functions.name: allocate_token_budget
functions.description: Distributes a total token budget across contexts proportionally by business_weight using a floor-then-proportional algorithm with largest-remainder rounding. Algorithm: (a) Compute minimum floor allocation per context (floor_tokens = max(1, total_budget // (len(contexts) * 10))). (b) If sum of floor allocations exceeds total_budget, apply pro-rata reduction so sum equals total_budget. (c) Distribute the remainder (total_budget - sum_of_floors) proportionally by business_weight. (d) Use largest-remainder method (Hare quota) for integer rounding so the sum of allocated_tokens equals total_budget exactly. This is a pure function.

inputs.name: total_budget
inputs.description: The total number of tokens to distribute across all contexts. Must be >= 0.

inputs.name: contexts
inputs.description: The contexts to allocate budget to. Must be non-empty.

error_data.message: contexts must be non-empty; cannot allocate budget to zero contexts.

error_cases.name: duplicate_context_ids
error_cases.condition: Two or more contexts share the same context_id

error_data.message: Duplicate context_id found: {context_id}. All context_ids must be unique.

error_cases.name: invalid_weight_in_context
error_cases.condition: Any context has a business_weight outside [0.0, 1.0]

error_cases.name: zero_total_weight
error_cases.condition: Sum of all business_weights is 0.0 (should not happen with floor of 0.1, but guarded)

error_data.message: Total business_weight sum is 0.0; cannot compute proportional allocation.

preconditions: All contexts have valid business_weight values (in [0.1, 1.0] after validation).
All context_ids are unique within the input list.
postconditions: len(result) == len(contexts)
sum(a.allocated_tokens for a in result) == total_budget
for all a in result: a.allocated_tokens >= 0
for all a in result: a.proportion >= 0.0 and a.proportion <= 1.0
sum(a.proportion for a in result) is approximately 1.0 (within floating-point epsilon) when total_budget > 0
Each result element's context_id matches exactly one input context's context_id.
Each result element's business_weight equals the corresponding input context's business_weight.
If total_budget == 0, all allocated_tokens are 0 and all proportions are 0.0.
If all contexts have equal business_weight, all allocations are equal (within +/- 1 token due to rounding).

functions.name: compute_business_weight
functions.description: Computes a business weight from four normalized input signals: signal frequency, author seniority, channel gravity, and engagement velocity. Returns a clamped value in [0.1, 1.0]. This is a pure function consumed by Context construction upstream — it is NOT part of the routing/budget execution path. Consumers of routing and budget functions receive pre-computed weights.

inputs.name: seniority
inputs.description: Author seniority score from identity resolver, normalized to [0.0, 1.0].

inputs.name: gravity
inputs.description: Channel gravity learned from response patterns, normalized to [0.0, 1.0].

error_data.message: All inputs must be finite numbers.

preconditions: All inputs are finite floats in [0.0, 1.0].
postconditions: result >= 0.1 and result <= 1.0
If all inputs are 0.0, result == 0.1 (operational floor).
If all inputs are 1.0, result == 1.0.
Result is deterministic: same inputs always produce same output.

invariants: business_weight MUST NOT appear in any familiarity score computation, resonance check, or acceptance threshold evaluation. It affects evaluation ORDER only.
Stop-on-first-accept semantics are preserved: business_weight changes which context is evaluated first, not whether a context is accepted.
All business_weight values on Context and WorkerNode are in [0.1, 1.0] after validation (operational floor enforced).
Raw business_weight values in [0.0, 0.1) are clamped to 0.1; values outside [0.0, 1.0] are rejected.
The default business_weight is 0.5 when not explicitly set.
Routing snapshots are immutable: once created, ordered_contexts must not be re-sorted or mutated mid-round.
Token budget allocation always sums to exactly total_budget (no tokens lost or created).
Token budget allocation uses largest-remainder rounding to ensure integer sum equality with total_budget.
When floor allocations exceed total_budget, pro-rata reduction is applied so sum still equals total_budget.
All functions in this contract are pure: no side effects, no external service dependencies, fully deterministic for the same inputs.
compute_business_weight is consumed upstream at Context construction time; routing and budget functions receive pre-computed weights.
Priority queue ordering uses (-business_weight, insertion_counter) tuples to achieve descending weight order with stable FIFO tiebreaking.
